name: J-Dawgs AI Tool Store — Full Catalog
source: J-Dawgs Agent Exchange agentJson catalog (membership, counts, prices — the source of truth the builders maintain), enriched from the AI Tool Store ai-catalog block (category, takes_in, hands_back, status, offer URLs) and the Lane 6 share-record URL resolutions (~/workspace/mcp/jdawgs-mcp/build_catalog.py)
counts_note: Counts mirror the J-Dawgs Agent Exchange header verbatim. The Exchange lists every entry below; its header counts the tools built by J-Dawgs — the flagship free Almost-JSON Repair Bench Lite edition is carried in the list with its live URL.

unlimited_pass.name: J-Dawgs Unlimited Pass
unlimited_pass.terms: One-time payment. Unlimited use of every priced tool in the store, including all future tools.

everything_stack.name: The Everything Stack
everything_stack.terms: One full pass through all priced tools on the shelf.

tools.name: Almost-JSON Repair Bench — Free Lite Edition
tools.description: Free lite edition of the J-Dawgs Almost-JSON Repair Bench — repair near-JSON safely in your browser, now with a damage summary on every repair, free — now also with a JSON Lines / NDJSON mode with a per-line damage receipt (bad lines kept in place and marked, never dropped). Now with a Repair Diff & Validation Receipt: every change listed by line with before/after fragments, a VALID / STILL INVALID badge from re-parsing the output, and a downloadable receipt. Now also with a Streaming Fragments mode: per-fragment receipts and mid-token cut locations — truncated streams are reported, never completed

tools.name: Hands Job Poster™
tools.description: Build a ready-to-send Human Hands job post with the pay math done — now with storm/weather-damage property checks and in-person business verification visits, a live pay calculator (worker keeps 100%, payer adds 15%), and a per-category photo-proof checklist builder — now also scores post completeness, warns on duplicate drafts, and emits a copyable worker brief — now also with a Fair-Pay Sanity Check: labeled time estimates per category, an implied hourly rate from worker-received pay, a LIKELY TOO LOW / FAIR RANGE / GENEROUS verdict, and a pay line in the Worker Brief — now also with Ambiguity Flags: vague wording quoted with rewrite suggestions, a CLEAR / A FEW GAPS / TOO VAGUE TO PRICE verdict, and the flags carried into the Worker Brief — now also with a built-in Scam-Pattern & Safety Self-Check: gift-card, crypto, wire-transfer, password-ask, check-cashing and reshipping patterns named with the quoted phrases that triggered them, and its READY verdict is blocked until HIGH warnings are acknowledged — plus a per-category worker-safety checklist. It now also generates a category-specific photo-proof checklist in every post, and blocks READY until a category is chosen.
tools.takes_in: Task, details, category, location, pay_usd, photo_proof_required, and agent
tools.hands_back: Ready-to-POST JSON validated against the inbox API rules — worker pay (100% of the posted price), the 15% payer fee, and the total from the live pay calculator, plus the job's per-category photo-proof checklist, a job-post completeness score with duplicate-draft warnings, and a copyable worker brief, a Scam-Pattern & Safety Self-Check that names scam patterns with their quoted phrases and blocks the READY verdict until HIGH warnings are acknowledged, and a per-category worker-safety checklist

tools.name: J-Dawgs Action-Item Accountability Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a meeting’s action-item list plus its follow-up log; every item graded accounted-done, done-with-no-evidence, overdue, orphan, or ownerless, with a carry-over list for the next agenda
tools.takes_in: The action-item list from your meeting notes — each item with its owner and due date where given — plus the follow-up log: what was reported done, shown as evidence, or chased since the meeting
tools.hands_back: Every item graded — accounted done, done-claimed with no evidence, overdue, orphan (never followed up), or ownerless — each grade with the log line behind it, plus a copyable carry-over list for the next agenda

tools.name: J-Dawgs Address Deliverability Pre-Flight Auditor™
tools.description: Pre-flights pasted US addresses before a worker or package is sent: missing house numbers, ZIP-to-state mismatches, PO Box carrier notes, and formatting duplicates — READY / REVIEW / FIX BEFORE SENDING per address. Structure and consistency only; does not verify any address exists.
tools.takes_in: A pasted list of US addresses — one per line — about to be handed to a worker, a delivery, or a package
tools.hands_back: A per-address verdict — READY / REVIEW / FIX BEFORE SENDING — with missing house numbers, ZIP-to-state mismatches, PO Box carrier notes, and formatting duplicates named; structure and consistency only — it does not verify any address exists

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Config Checker™
tools.description: Catch silent mistakes in an agent's config before they cost a run — now with a referenced-vs-declared cross-check and a Safe-Fix Draft export — now also with MCP Server Block Validation
tools.takes_in: An agent config: YAML, SKILL.md or agent frontmatter, or JSON
tools.hands_back: A staged report: what parsed, every flagged mistake with its line number and a plain-words fix, and an honest note on anything outside the checker's YAML subset that couldn't be fully checked

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Failure Postmortem Builder™
tools.description: Turn a failed run into a structured postmortem with causes and fixes
tools.takes_in: A failed run's transcript, plus the intended outcome and the actual outcome
tools.hands_back: A structured postmortem: a summary, a timeline with quoted lines, suspected causes rated STRONG or POSSIBLE (never CERTAIN), impact measured from transcript counts, a fix checklist, a do-not-repeat checklist, and an explicit unverified-items section

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Handoff Packer™
tools.description: Turn run notes into a structured handoff brief for the next agent — now also extracts critical items with their source sections and generates a copyable read-back checklist — now also with a Size Budget & Truncation Risk panel
tools.takes_in: Messy notes from an agent run — logs, fragments, half-finished threads, scattered observations
tools.hands_back: A structured handoff brief: what's done, what's pending, blockers, decisions made, unverified claims flagged as unverified, and a do-not-repeat checklist — with the critical items extracted alongside their source sections, plus a copyable read-back checklist, a Handoff Size Budget & Truncation Risk panel, and a core-brief mode

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Loop Detective™
tools.description: Find repeat and ping-pong loops wasting steps in agent transcripts — now also names the first divergence point and exports a circuit-breaker JSON config — now also projects repeat-burn and emits a one-line incident summary
tools.takes_in: An agent run transcript — the tool calls an agent made, in order, with their results
tools.hands_back: Every loop pattern found — exact-repeat, near-duplicate, and ping-pong tool calls — with each failure classified as retryable or deterministic, and a stop / pivot / escalate verdict for each pattern, the first divergence point where the run started looping, and a copyable circuit-breaker JSON config derived from the transcript

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Permission-Use & Scope-Creep Auditor™
tools.description: Audits permissions AFTER a run: grant list vs action log → permission receipt with within-scope actions, scope-creep blockers with spend arithmetic, and granted-but-unused revoke candidates. Verdict: WITHIN GRANTED SCOPE / SCOPE CREEP FOUND / CANNOT FULLY VERIFY
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: the permissions the agent was granted, and the log of actions it actually took
tools.hands_back: A permission receipt — actions WITHIN SCOPE with the deciding grant quoted, SCOPE CREEP blockers named (writes outside granted roots, ungranted hosts, spend over cap with the arithmetic), granted-but-unused permissions as revoke candidates, and one verdict: WITHIN GRANTED SCOPE / SCOPE CREEP FOUND / CANNOT FULLY VERIFY

tools.name: J-Dawgs Agent Trace Secret Sweeper™
tools.description: Scan transcripts and logs for leaked secrets and get a redacted copy — now also detects JWT-shaped tokens graded by the sensitive claims they carry, and opens with a per-severity summary of everything found
tools.takes_in: A pasted agent transcript, trace, or log — the whole text, as-is
tools.hands_back: Every likely secret found, each with its type, line number, severity, and a masked preview only — plus a redacted copy of the full text with the secrets replaced, safe to share

tools.name: J-Dawgs Almost-JSON Repair Bench™
tools.description: Repair near-JSON safely, with a change log, never inventing data
tools.takes_in: Raw AI model output that was supposed to be JSON — fences, prose, and all
tools.hands_back: The diagnosed failure class, the repaired valid JSON, and a change log listing every fix — or, for truncated output, a plain report that it was cut off and needs the model to continue

tools.name: J-Dawgs Ansible Playbook Risk Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted Ansible playbook — destructive tasks, privilege, unpinned remote code, plaintext secrets by key name only — into one run verdict. ansible-lint stops at style inside a repo; ours grades run-safety anywhere.
tools.takes_in: A pasted Ansible playbook — the full YAML, plays, tasks, handlers and all
tools.hands_back: One run verdict with every risky task located — destructive commands, privilege escalation, unpinned remote code — and plaintext secrets flagged by key name only, values never shown

tools.name: J-Dawgs Answer Flip & Sycophancy Auditor™
tools.description: Paste an AI's original answer, the pushback it got, and its revised answer; see claim by claim what flipped, what held, and whether the pushback contained any new evidence that could justify the change
tools.takes_in: Three texts: an AI's original answer, the pushback it received, and its revised answer
tools.hands_back: A claim-by-claim ledger — what flipped, what held, what was softened or dropped — and, for each change, a judgment on whether the pushback contained any new evidence that could justify it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Answer-to-Trace Evidence Linker™
tools.description: Checks every factual claim in a draft agent answer against the tool-output trace from the same run and flags unsupported or contradicted claims with the evidence shown
tools.takes_in: A draft agent answer, plus the tool-output trace from the same run — the tool results, readings, and outputs the answer was built from
tools.hands_back: A per-claim verdict table — GROUNDED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, or CONTRADICTS TRACE — with the trace evidence quoted for each claim, an overall DO NOT SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / GROUNDED verdict, and the draft itself returned with unsupported claims flagged inline, never deleted

tools.name: J-Dawgs API Deprecation & Sunset Radar™
tools.description: Paste deprecation notices and the API versions you call; get a dated sunset timeline and a migration priority order. No notice found never means safe — versions with no notice are flagged as unknown, not cleared
tools.takes_in: Pasted deprecation and sunset notices — emails, changelog entries, docs pages — plus the endpoints and API versions you actually call
tools.hands_back: A dated sunset timeline — every called endpoint and version with its sunset date and days remaining — and a migration priority list ordered by deadline and how much you call it; anything with no notice is marked UNCONFIRMED, never safe

tools.name: J-Dawgs API Endpoint Reality Checker™
tools.description: Grades planned API calls against the API's own spec: exists, wrong method, invented path with closest suggestion, deprecated, missing required params
tools.takes_in: The planned API calls — method and path, with any parameters — plus the API's own spec: an OpenAPI document or the endpoint list it publishes
tools.hands_back: A grade per planned call — EXISTS, WRONG METHOD, INVENTED PATH with the closest real endpoint named, DEPRECATED, or MISSING REQUIRED PARAMS — and the corrected call list

tools.name: J-Dawgs API Schema Drift Detector™
tools.description: Compare two API schemas and flag breaking changes
tools.takes_in: Two shapes: the API response shape your agent was built against, and the JSON the API just returned
tools.hands_back: A per-field findings table that separates BREAKING drift — missing fields, type changes, enum violations, suspected restructures — from harmless ADDITIVE changes, plus a plain-language fix list

tools.name: J-Dawgs Argument Provenance Checker™
tools.description: Classifies every planned tool-call argument value as Found in source / Derived / Transformed / Invented against pasted source context, escalates invented sensitive arguments, and outputs a cleaned call
tools.takes_in: Your source context — the text the call is supposed to be built from — plus the planned tool calls with their argument values
tools.hands_back: Every argument value classified Found in source / Derived (with the derivation shown) / Transformed / Invented, invented sensitive arguments — email, amount, ID, date — escalated, and a cleaned call with the invented values stripped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Arithmetic & Totals Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a draft report, invoice, or quote; every written equation, line-item total, subtotal-plus-tax chain, and percentage claim in it is recomputed with real arithmetic and flagged where the draft's math does not hold
tools.takes_in: A draft with numbers in it — a report, invoice, quote, or estimate carrying written equations, line items, totals, tax chains, or percentage claims
tools.hands_back: Every equation, line-item total, subtotal-plus-tax chain, and percentage claim recomputed with real arithmetic — each flagged where the draft's math does not hold, with the draft figure, the recomputed figure, and the difference

tools.name: J-Dawgs Backup Manifest & Restore Proof Auditor™
tools.description: Cross-checks a backup manifest against a restore-drill log; refuses RESTORE PROVEN without a recent, content-verified, checksummed restore
tools.takes_in: Three pasted lists: your expected-coverage list (the datasets that must be backed up), your backup manifest, and your restore-drill log
tools.hands_back: One verdict — RESTORE PROVEN, or the refusal with its reasons — with every coverage gap, stale backup, missing checksum, and failed or old-snapshot drill named by dataset and line

tools.name: J-Dawgs Blank Page Diagnostician™
tools.description: Paste a blank page's URL and HTML/JS source; get a ranked diagnosis — missing mount node, unparseable embedded JSON, script-before-DOM, unbalanced code, render-blocking head scripts — each with evidence and the exact fix, plus a clean bill of what passed. Leads with the honest platform answer for Muse share links
tools.takes_in: A page URL plus the page's HTML/JS source, pasted — the markup and scripts behind the blank page
tools.hands_back: A ranked diagnosis — every likely cause with the exact evidence from the source and the concrete fix for each — plus a clean bill listing what passed; for Muse share links, the honest first answer that the white screen is Muse's loading shell, not a broken page

tools.name: J-Dawgs Blocker Triage & Minimal Ask Builder™
tools.description: Classify blockers as self-serve / human judgment / human hands / external wait / not-a-blocker and build one minimal human ask, with an approval-overload flag
tools.takes_in: A blocked plan — the plan text with its blockers, pasted as-is
tools.hands_back: Every blocker classified SELF-SERVE, NEEDS-HUMAN-JUDGMENT, NEEDS-HUMAN-HANDS, EXTERNAL-WAIT, or NOT-A-BLOCKER with the signal words that decided it, an APPROVAL OVERLOAD flag when more than 3 items head to the human, and one copyable Minimal Ask containing only the human items, credential values stripped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Browser Selector Fragility Auditor™
tools.description: Scores locators and fixed waits in browser-automation code for fragility and produces a worst-first rewrite plan toward resilient locators
tools.takes_in: Browser automation code — Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium — with the locators, selectors, and waits it uses to find and drive page elements
tools.hands_back: A fragility score for every locator and fixed wait in the code, ranked worst-first, with the brittle pattern named for each and a rewrite plan toward resilient locators — roles, labels, and test IDs instead of paths and positions

tools.name: J-Dawgs Bug Report Reproducibility Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a draft bug report; get one verdict (READY TO FILE / FILE WITH FIXES / NOT REPRODUCIBLE YET), per-section grades, and a file-ready skeleton that keeps every fact and marks only genuinely missing pieces — never invents steps or versions.
tools.takes_in: A pasted draft bug report — whatever state it is currently in
tools.hands_back: One verdict — READY TO FILE / FILE WITH FIXES / NOT REPRODUCIBLE YET — per-section grades, and a file-ready skeleton marking only the genuinely missing pieces, with nothing invented to fill them

tools.name: J-Dawgs Cache Key Collision & Tenant-Leak Auditor™
tools.description: Audits cache key patterns and sample keys for collisions, tenant-scoping gaps, raw-input keys, and TTL problems — the class of bug that serves one tenant another tenant's cached data
tools.takes_in: Your cache key patterns plus sample keys as actually written — and which caches are shared between tenants
tools.hands_back: Every collision flagged with the keys involved, shared-cache keys missing tenant scoping named as tenant-leak risks, raw user input in keys called out, and TTL risks listed — each with the fix

tools.name: J-Dawgs Calendar Invite Integrity Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted .ics calendar invite: missing UID/DTSTAMP, floating times, undefined TZIDs, duplicate UIDs, open-ended RRULEs, and overlaps; one import verdict
tools.takes_in: A pasted .ics (iCalendar) file — a single invite or a whole calendar export
tools.hands_back: One import verdict — IMPORT, FIX FIRST, or DO NOT IMPORT — with every defect named by event: missing UID or DTSTAMP, floating times, undefined TZIDs, duplicate UIDs, open-ended RRULEs, and overlapping events

tools.name: J-Dawgs Capability Gap Mapper™
tools.description: Pre-flight capability check: paste an agent's available tools and a task's required capabilities (MUST:/NICE:) — each requirement mapped COVERED / PARTIAL / MISSING with matched words quoted, a visible synonym table, READY / READY WITH WORKAROUNDS / NOT READY verdict, and a copyable brief naming the exact gaps to flag before starting
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: the tools the agent actually has — names, with a line on what each one does — and the capabilities the task needs, one per line, marked MUST: or NICE:
tools.hands_back: A requirement-by-requirement map — every MUST: and NICE: graded COVERED / PARTIAL / MISSING with the matched words quoted as evidence, the synonym table it matched on shown in the open, one READY / READY WITH WORKAROUNDS / NOT READY verdict, and a copyable pre-flight brief naming exactly which missing MUSTs to flag to the user up front

tools.name: J-Dawgs Catalog Count Reconciliation Auditor™
tools.description: Recomputes a catalog's claimed headline counts and price sums from the underlying data and flags drift to the cent — and returns a corrected claims block.
tools.takes_in: A pasted catalog's item data — the listings with their statuses and prices — plus the headline claims exactly as published
tools.hands_back: A reconciliation report — every claimed count and price sum recomputed from the items, drift flagged to the cent with claimed-vs-actual side by side — and a corrected claims block ready to paste in

tools.name: J-Dawgs Certificate Chain & Expiry Auditor™
tools.description: SSL testers need a live public hostname and stop at a grade; this audits pasted certificate text offline — expiry bands, SAN coverage for your expected hostnames with true wildcard rules, and leaf-first chain order — and returns one deploy verdict
tools.takes_in: Pasted certificate text — a PEM or text dump of the leaf and its chain — plus the hostnames the certificate has to cover
tools.hands_back: One deploy verdict, the expiry band for every certificate in the pasted text, SAN coverage for each expected hostname with true wildcard rules applied, and a leaf-first chain-order check with every gap named

tools.name: J-Dawgs Changelog & Version Honesty Auditor™
tools.description: Cross-checks old version, new version, changelog, and change list against semver, names undocumented changes and unbacked claims, and suggests the honest version
tools.takes_in: The old version, the new version, the changelog, and the list of changes that actually shipped
tools.hands_back: One verdict — HONEST RELEASE, FIX THE NOTES, or MISLEADING RELEASE — with the implied bump set against the bump the changes required, undocumented changes and unbacked claims named, a suggested honest version, and a copyable report

tools.name: J-Dawgs Chunk Boundary Damage Bench™
tools.description: Benches two RAG chunking strategies side by side on a pasted document and scores boundary damage — mid-sentence cuts, broken code fences, orphaned headings, severed procedures, tiny fragments — before you buy embeddings
tools.takes_in: A document to be chunked for embedding or retrieval — plus the chunk size and overlap to test, or two named strategies to compare
tools.hands_back: Both chunk sets side by side: every chunk with its boundary-damage flags, the size spread per strategy, and a verdict per strategy — which one damages this document less, and where

tools.name: J-Dawgs Citation Grounding Checker™
tools.description: Checks each cited claim against its pasted source excerpt — quotes, numbers, names, placeholder citations — to catch vibe citing. Now with a Number & Unit Consistency pass (scale/currency normalization, percent-form mismatches, cross-unit conversions with math shown)
tools.takes_in: Each claim with its citation and the source excerpt it rests on
tools.hands_back: A check of whether the excerpt actually carries the claim — verbatim quotes, numbers, and names verified against it, and placeholder DOIs flagged; it checks the excerpt you paste and does not browse the web

tools.name: J-Dawgs Claim Checker™
tools.description: Check a claim against its source text and get a verdict with evidence — now with a batch mode that scores many claims in one pass, with per-claim evidence-strength grades (STRONG/WEAK/NONE)
tools.takes_in: A claim, plus the source text it supposedly comes from
tools.hands_back: Supported, Partially supported, Not found in source, or Contradicted — with a detail breakdown, highlighted evidence quotes, and found / missing lists, plus a report you can copy or download

tools.name: J-Dawgs CODEOWNERS Coverage Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted CODEOWNERS file against a pasted file list: every file gets its deciding rule, unowned sensitive paths are flagged as blockers, stale rules that match nothing are named, and the audit returns one ownership verdict — FULLY OWNED / OWNED WITH GAPS / UNOWNED RISK.
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: the CODEOWNERS file and the repository's file list
tools.hands_back: A coverage report — every file with its deciding rule quoted, unowned sensitive paths flagged as blockers, stale rules named — and one ownership verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Command & Flag Hallucination Checker™
tools.description: Checks a proposed command's flags and subcommands against pasted --help/man text; invented surface named with closest-match suggestions; never executes anything; one verdict per command
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: a proposed command line, and the program's own --help output or man text to check it against
tools.hands_back: Every flag and subcommand checked against the reference — invented surface named NOT IN REFERENCE with the closest real flag suggested (labeled a suggestion), value problems and dangerous constructs flagged separately, and one verdict per command: MATCHES REFERENCE / FIX BEFORE RUNNING / DO NOT RUN

tools.name: J-Dawgs Commit History Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted git log: Conventional Commits format, vague subjects, breaking changes with no marker, fixup/squash leakage, duplicates — one publish verdict. Commitlint-style linters check one message inside a repo; this audits a whole pasted history anywhere and flags undocumented breaking changes and leakage, not just format
tools.takes_in: A pasted git log — the commit subjects, and bodies where you have them, exactly as the history is about to be published or shared
tools.hands_back: Every fault named by commit — Conventional Commits format failures, vague subjects, breaking changes with no marker, fixup/squash leakage, and duplicate subjects — and one publish verdict for the whole history: SAFE TO PUBLISH / PUBLISH WITH FIXES / DO NOT PUBLISH

tools.name: J-Dawgs Commitment Date & SLA Promise Auditor™
tools.description: Extracts deadline promises from drafts; flags past dates, impossible lead times, and weekend/blackout collisions; marks "soon" as unverifiable
tools.takes_in: A draft message containing date or deadline commitments, today's date, and — where they apply — the required lead time, business-day rules, and blackout dates
tools.hands_back: Every promise extracted and checked one by one: past dates, weekend and blackout-date promises, lead-time violations, and vague commitments like ‘soon’, each flagged with the quoted wording and a corrected date or phrasing

tools.name: J-Dawgs Compaction Loss Auditor™
tools.description: Compares original agent notes against a compacted summary and returns KEPT / SOFTENED / LOST for every number, date, name, decision and constraint, plus a copyable rescue list of what compaction dropped
tools.takes_in: An agent's original notes, plus the compacted summary that replaced them — both pasted as-is
tools.hands_back: Every number, date, name, decision and constraint from the original classified as KEPT, SOFTENED or LOST, plus a copyable rescue list of everything compaction dropped

tools.name: J-Dawgs Compose Stack Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted Docker Compose file per service — privileged, Docker socket, masked secrets, exposed databases, cross-service risks — and returns one ship verdict with a fix list, no install, no Docker
tools.takes_in: One pasted Docker Compose file — the exact Compose YAML you are about to deploy
tools.hands_back: One ship verdict — SAFE TO DEPLOY, DEPLOY WITH FIXES, or DO NOT DEPLOY — with per-service findings with line numbers, severity counts, and a copyable report carrying the fix list

tools.name: J-Dawgs Connector Credential & Egress Verifier™
tools.description: Paste a failed connector or API call's error output plus its setup facts; get the failure classified — placeholder token unswapped, missing credential, placement mismatch, unregistered host, insufficient key scope, malformed or masked credential, account not activated — with a fix checklist and a first-time setup preflight list
tools.takes_in: The error output of a failed connector or API call — its HTTP status and error body — plus the setup facts: the auth scheme, where the credential was placed, and whether the provider host was registered for the connector
tools.hands_back: One named diagnosis with the evidence quoted from the pasted error, an ordered fix checklist specific to that failure class, and a preflight checklist for first-time connector setup

tools.name: J-Dawgs Consent Scope Auditor™
tools.description: Extracts granted/denied/conditional consent from a pasted history and checks each planned action — covered, denied, conditional, not covered, or scope creep
tools.takes_in: A pasted history of what the user said — the grants, denials, and time-boxes in their own words — plus the actions you plan to take
tools.hands_back: Each planned action marked covered, denied, time-boxed (with the window), or never granted — with scope creep named where a plan stretches a grant past what was said

tools.name: J-Dawgs Container Build Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Install-first Dockerfile linters stop at per-line style rules; ours also grades the runtime posture (root user, secrets in build args, remote-script pipes) and returns one ship verdict with a fix list — no install
tools.takes_in: A pasted Dockerfile — plus the build args and the .dockerignore, if you have them
tools.hands_back: One ship verdict — SHIP, FIX FIRST, or DO NOT SHIP — with every finding graded, the runtime posture scored, and a fix list in the order to work it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Context Budget Planner™
tools.description: Budget an agent's context window and get a trim plan — now also produces an ordered compaction plan and a section-share breakdown
tools.takes_in: A prompt in zones — system text, instructions, examples, documents, history — plus the context window size it has to fit
tools.hands_back: A token estimate for each zone, the total against the window, a FITS / TIGHT / OVER BUDGET verdict, a prioritized trim plan naming what to cut first, an ordered compaction plan — numbered cuts with the savings at each step and the running headroom after it — and a section-share breakdown showing each section's share of the window

tools.name: J-Dawgs Cookie Consent & Declaration Auditor™
tools.description: Cross-checks a pasted actual cookie inventory against the pasted consent declaration: undeclared cookies flagged as blockers, stale declarations, category mismatches, and long expiries — and returns one ship verdict plus a corrected declaration draft.
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: the actual cookie inventory (names, expiries, and categories as the site sets them) and the published consent declaration
tools.hands_back: A cross-check report — undeclared cookies flagged as blockers, stale declarations, category mismatches, and long expiries named — one ship verdict, and a corrected declaration draft that matches the inventory

tools.name: J-Dawgs Correction Persistence Checker™
tools.description: Checks mid-task corrections against the final output and parallel outputs: APPLIED / REVERTED / DID NOT SPREAD, with a fix list
tools.takes_in: The mid-task correction log — what was corrected, from what, to what — plus the final output and, where they exist, the parallel worker outputs
tools.hands_back: A verdict per correction — APPLIED, REVERTED with the old value quoted where it still stands, or DID NOT SPREAD — and a copyable fix list for everything that didn't stick

tools.name: J-Dawgs Correction Quality Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a correction draft against the original wrong statement: is the error named, the corrected value supplied, any new figure unsourced, any hedge re-softening the fix — one send/don't-send verdict
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: the original wrong statement, and the correction draft about to go out
tools.hands_back: A check-by-check audit — error named or not, corrected value supplied or not, every new figure flagged sourced or unsourced, hedges that re-soften the fix quoted — and one verdict: SEND / SEND WITH FIXES / DO NOT SEND

tools.name: J-Dawgs CORS Policy & Preflight Auditor™
tools.description: Cross-checks pasted CORS response headers against the exact described request: wildcard-with-credentials fatal combo, preflight coverage, Vary/cache risks — one pass/blocked verdict
tools.takes_in: Two pastes: the CORS response headers your server sends, and the exact request you need to make — its origin, whether it carries credentials, its method, and its custom headers
tools.hands_back: The headers cross-checked against the described request — the wildcard-with-credentials fatal combination named on sight, preflight coverage walked header by header (methods and custom headers), Vary and cache risks flagged, the exact blocking line named — and one verdict: PASS / BLOCKED

tools.name: J-Dawgs RRULE Recurrence Auditor™

tools.name: J-Dawgs SBOM Completeness & License Auditor™

tools.name: J-Dawgs Schedule Time Pre-Flight Checker™
tools.description: Validates a planned local date/time/IANA timezone before scheduling: nonexistent DST-gap times, ambiguous fall-back times, weekday mismatches and abbreviation traps, with cross-zone conversions — now with a Batch Audit mode for many scheduled times at once, with per-line verdicts and one copyable report

tools.name: J-Dawgs Schema Inference Forge™

tools.name: J-Dawgs Set-Cookie & Session Header Auditor™

tools.name: J-Dawgs Shell Script Safety Auditor™

tools.name: J-Dawgs Silent Result Triage Bench™
tools.description: Triages a batch of tool results against declared expectations: EMPTY, PARTIAL, SEMANTIC MISMATCH, plus a downstream contamination map

tools.name: J-Dawgs Sitemap & Robots Agent-Access Auditor™

tools.hands_back: Per-agent access for ten well-known crawlers, each verdict with the deciding robots.txt rule quoted; every sitemap entry your own rules block, named; and a fix list — computed from the pasted text alone, nothing fetched

tools.name: J-Dawgs Social Preview & Meta Head Auditor™
tools.description: Social preview checkers fetch a live URL and only show a preview; ours audits a pasted head offline before publish — OG/Twitter/canonical completeness, length bands, mismatches and relative-image blockers — and returns one share verdict
tools.takes_in: A pasted page head — the OG, Twitter card, and canonical meta tags exactly as they will publish
tools.hands_back: A completeness, length-band, and mismatch report for the OG / Twitter / canonical tags, any relative-image blockers named, and one verdict: SHARE-READY / FIX BEFORE SHARING / DO NOT SHARE YET

tools.name: J-Dawgs SQL Migration Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted SQL migration and its optional rollback entirely offline — destructive operations, lock risks, and rollback gaps flagged by line, with one verdict and line-numbered fixes. It never connects to a database

tools.hands_back: One verdict — SAFE TO APPLY / APPLY WITH FIXES / DO NOT APPLY — with every destructive operation, lock risk, and rollback gap listed at its line number, each with the concrete fix to make before the migration runs

tools.name: J-Dawgs SQL Pre-Flight Guard™
tools.description: Audits SQL an agent is about to run before anything executes: blocks unscoped DELETE/UPDATE, DROP/TRUNCATE, and tautology WHERE clauses in Production mode, with a safer-plan checklist per flagged statement
tools.takes_in: The SQL an agent is about to run — one statement or a whole script — plus the mode it will run in: production, staging, or unstated
tools.hands_back: A statement-by-statement audit: each statement classified, the dangerous ones flagged or blocked with the exact pattern that tripped the flag, and a safer-plan checklist per flagged statement — what to add, scope, or verify before it may run

tools.name: J-Dawgs SSH Key & Authorized-Keys Auditor™
tools.description: Key scanners and ssh-keygen work one key at a time from an install; ours batch-audits a pasted authorized_keys file offline — decoded-blob algorithm match, RSA size grading, real SHA-256 fingerprints, duplicates named by line, risky options graded — and returns one access verdict.
tools.takes_in: One pasted authorized_keys file — or a batch of SSH public keys, one per line
tools.hands_back: A per-key audit — decoded-blob algorithm match, RSA size grade, the real SHA-256 fingerprint, duplicates named by line, risky options (forced commands, port-forwarding, agent-forwarding, no-pty) graded — and one access verdict for the whole file

tools.name: J-Dawgs Stack Trace Triage Bench™
tools.description: Groups a pasted error-log blob by root signature — ranked groups, a first-error callout, and LIKELY SYMPTOM candidates labeled as evidence, not proof — with a copyable report and JSON export
tools.takes_in: A pasted error log or stack-trace blob — the whole messy output, as it came: application logs, worker output, CI failures, timestamps and all
tools.hands_back: Ranked error groups by root signature — each with its count, first and last lines, and representative trace — LIKELY SYMPTOM labels on the probable fallout, a first-error callout, and a copyable triage report plus a JSON export

tools.name: J-Dawgs Stale Evidence & Freshness Checker™
tools.description: Checks a draft against its sources' retrieval dates and cache status, flags stale or undated evidence presented as current, and inserts honest "as of" qualifiers
tools.takes_in: A draft answer, plus the sources behind it — each with the date it was retrieved and whether it came back live or served from cache
tools.hands_back: A label for every currency claim in the draft — FRESH or STALE-BACKED — with stale, undated, and cached-as-live evidence flagged, and the draft returned with honest “as of” qualifiers inserted and every fact left exactly as it was

tools.name: J-Dawgs Structured Output Conformance Bench™
tools.description: Batch-validates LLM JSON outputs against a JSON Schema, classifying every failure by type with exact paths and a conformance rate — now also with a Fix-First Summary: failures grouped by schema path, one fix per top path, and a highest-leverage headline naming the single fix that clears the most failures
tools.takes_in: Many LLM JSON outputs, pasted as a batch, plus the one JSON Schema they were all supposed to follow
tools.hands_back: Every failure classified by type — missing required, wrong type, enum miss, extra field, truncated, not JSON — with the exact path of each failure, a conformance rate for the batch, and the single most common fix needed; classification only, it never invents values

tools.name: J-Dawgs Subagent Brief Stress-Tester™
tools.description: Scores a subagent delegation brief for completeness and drift risks and generates a tightened brief
tools.takes_in: A delegation brief — the task text you are about to hand to a subagent, pasted as-is
tools.hands_back: A score against 10 completeness elements with each missing element named, the drift risks and contradictions flagged with the lines that cause them, and a tightened brief generated from yours, ready to send

tools.name: J-Dawgs Support Ticket Triage & Escalation Auditor™
tools.description: Grades a pasted inbound support ticket before any reply — missing diagnostics, urgency/security signals, unsupported promises in a draft — into ANSWER NOW / ASK FIRST / ESCALATE NOW plus a reply checklist that never invents facts.
tools.takes_in: A pasted inbound support ticket — plus, optionally, the draft reply about to go back
tools.hands_back: One triage verdict — ANSWER NOW / ASK FIRST / ESCALATE NOW — the missing diagnostics named, urgency and security signals quoted, and a reply checklist that flags unsupported promises and never invents facts

tools.name: J-Dawgs Suppression & Opt-Out Honor Checker™
tools.description: Cross-checks a send list against suppression/opt-out lists incl. normalized variants and blocked domains; returns the clean set with a full removal ledger
tools.takes_in: A planned send list — email addresses and/or phone numbers — plus the suppression and opt-out lists it has to honor
tools.hands_back: Only the clean set, safe to send — plus a removal ledger naming every address taken out and the exact match or variant that removed it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Systemd Unit Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted systemd unit file — root/sandboxing/restart-loop posture — into one run verdict. systemd-analyze grades a unit on a live host; ours audits a pasted unit anywhere and returns one verdict plus a line-numbered fix list.
tools.takes_in: A pasted systemd unit file — the whole [Unit] / [Service] / [Install] text, exactly as it would be deployed
tools.hands_back: One verdict — SAFE TO RUN / RUN WITH FIXES / DO NOT RUN YET — with a line-numbered fix list covering the user it runs as, sandboxing directives, and restart posture; secrets flagged by key name only, values never shown

tools.name: J-Dawgs Task Ambiguity Pre-Flight Checker™
tools.description: Flags underspecified tasks — missing done-definition, unresolved referents, vague quantities, missing constraints, conflicting directives — with ranked clarifying questions and a READY / ASSUMPTIONS LOGGED / ASK FIRST verdict
tools.takes_in: A task exactly as received — the message, ticket, or instruction text, unedited
tools.hands_back: Every gap flagged by type with the offending words quoted, one ranked clarifying question per gap, and a READY / ASSUMPTIONS LOGGED / ASK FIRST verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Terraform Plan Risk Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted Terraform plan (JSON or text) before apply: classifies CREATE / UPDATE / REPLACE / DESTROY, flags stateful destroys and replacements and IAM widening as BLOCKERs, and returns one verdict — SAFE TO APPLY / APPLY WITH CONFIRMATION / DO NOT APPLY YET.
tools.takes_in: A pasted Terraform plan — the JSON plan output or the human-readable text plan, before apply
tools.hands_back: A graded plan — changes classified CREATE / UPDATE / REPLACE / DESTROY, stateful destroys and replacements and IAM widening flagged as BLOCKERs, one apply verdict, and a confirmation checklist naming what a human must confirm before apply

tools.name: J-Dawgs Terraform Plan Safety Auditor™
tools.description: Paste a terraform show -json plan; destroy count headline, stateful delete/replace data-loss flags, world-open ingress and wildcard IAM flags, with tag-only noise separated — one apply verdict. The plan never leaves the device, and secret-looking values are masked
tools.takes_in: A terraform plan as JSON — the output of `terraform show -json` for the plan you are about to apply
tools.hands_back: One apply verdict led by the destroy count — every stateful delete or replace flagged as a data-loss risk, world-open ingress and wildcard IAM flagged by resource, tag-only changes counted separately as noise, and secret-looking values masked, never printed

tools.name: J-Dawgs Test Payload Forge™
tools.description: Forges valid and exactly-one-constraint-broken payload sets from a JSON Schema
tools.takes_in: A JSON Schema (draft-07) — plus, optionally, the fields or constraints you most want exercised
tools.hands_back: Two labeled payload sets: valid payloads that satisfy the schema, and invalid payloads that each violate exactly one named constraint — with the constraint each one breaks printed beside it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Timestamp & Timezone Forensics Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted list of mixed-format timestamps: epoch seconds-vs-milliseconds confusion, ambiguous slash dates flagged — never guessed — missing timezones, DST-nonexistent and DST-repeated times, duplicate instants, and out-of-order lines; normalizes every readable time to UTC plus the assumed zone.
tools.takes_in: A pasted list of mixed-format timestamps — epoch, ISO, slash dates, log lines — plus the timezone to assume where a line states none
tools.hands_back: Every line flagged by name — epoch seconds vs milliseconds confusion, ambiguous slash dates (flagged, never guessed), missing timezones, DST-nonexistent and DST-repeated local times, duplicate instants, out-of-order lines — and every readable time normalized to UTC plus your assumed zone

tools.name: J-Dawgs TOML Config Pre-Flight Auditor™
tools.description: Pre-flights pasted TOML with line numbers: duplicate tables/keys, mixed-type arrays, impossible calendar dates, unclosed strings — and never flags legal trailing commas
tools.takes_in: A pasted TOML config — pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, or an app config — exactly as it will ship
tools.hands_back: Findings by line number — duplicate tables and keys, mixed-type arrays, impossible calendar dates, unclosed strings — and one verdict: SAFE TO SHIP / SHIP WITH FIXES / DO NOT SHIP

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Call Pre-Flight Checker™
tools.description: Validate a planned tool call against its schema before running it — now also with Batch Mode: paste NDJSON or a JSON array, get one batch verdict plus a per-call table
tools.takes_in: A proposed tool call — the tool name and its arguments — plus the tool's JSON schema
tools.hands_back: A check report: tool-name match, missing required parameters, argument-type and enum violations, invented parameters, placeholder-looking values flagged, a destructive-operation banner on send / write / delete tools, and suggested corrected arguments

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Description Collision Checker™
tools.description: Scores every pair in a pasted set of tool definitions for description overlap, flags vague/name-echo descriptions and missing boundary conditions for confusable pairs (list-vs-search, draft-vs-publish), and drafts boundary rewrites labeled untested. Text analysis only — it cannot measure actual model tool picks
tools.takes_in: A set of tool definitions — JSON or plain text blocks — names and descriptions together
tools.hands_back: A pairwise overlap score for every pair of tools, flags on vague or name-echo descriptions, the missing boundary conditions for confusable pairs like list-vs-search and draft-vs-publish, and draft boundary rewrites labeled untested

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Distributor™
tools.description: Turn one tool's details into directory listings and launch posts
tools.takes_in: One tool's details — name, URL, pitch, description, category, and price model
tools.hands_back: A filled directory submission packet, social announcement posts, a machine-readable feed entry, and an agent-facing blurb — all ready to copy or download

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool Output Sanity Checker™
tools.description: Inspect a chain of tool outputs for silent failures before trusting them. Now exports a copyable first-bad-step incident snippet (secrets masked) and flags per-step output size and truncation suspects — suspicion labelled, never proof. Now also with a Baseline Shape Diff mode
tools.takes_in: A pasted chain of agent tool outputs, in the order the steps ran
tools.hands_back: Per-step flags — EMPTY, ERROR-IGNORED, PARTIAL, MALFORMED, SHAPE-DRIFT — the first bad step named, and an overall verdict: TRUSTWORTHY, SUSPECT, or DO NOT PROCEED

tools.name: J-Dawgs Tool-Result Truncation & Pagination Checker™
tools.description: Proves a tool result is whole before the agent answers — truncation, pagination, and completeness-claim checks
tools.takes_in: A tool result as returned — the items or text, any count or total the result or the call promised, and any pagination fields it carries — plus, optionally, the draft answer you are about to give from it
tools.hands_back: A wholeness verdict on the result — WHOLE, TRUNCATED, PAGINATED (more pages exist), or COUNT MISMATCH — with the exact signal each call rests on, plus flags on any draft-answer sentence that claims completeness the data doesn't support

tools.name: J-Dawgs Trademark Cost Calculator™
tools.description: Work out USPTO trademark filing costs before filing — now with a portfolio mode that plans up to 5 marks, with per-mark fee lines and a staged filing order
tools.takes_in: Number of marks, classes per mark, the filing route, and any surcharges that apply
tools.hands_back: The USPTO filing total with a line-by-line breakdown of the fees and surcharges behind it

tools.name: J-Dawgs Transcript-to-Runbook Extractor™
tools.description: Mines a successful agent transcript into a reusable runbook: steps, retries collapsed, decision branches, variables, definition of done
tools.takes_in: A successful agent run's transcript — the tool calls, the retries, the branch points, and the final result
tools.hands_back: A reusable runbook: ordered steps with retries collapsed, decision branches with their triggers, the variables to fill in, and a definition of done

tools.name: J-Dawgs Uncertainty & Hedge Auditor™
tools.description: Flags overconfident claims, unsupported numbers, and fake verification wording in draft agent answers, and rewrites an honest version
tools.takes_in: A draft agent answer, pasted as-is — the exact text you are about to send
tools.hands_back: Every unearned-confidence claim flagged — absolute claims with no evidence, numbers with no source, “verified” without saying what was checked, and strong claims quietly walked back later — plus an honest rewrite that only adds uncertainty wording, never facts

tools.name: J-Dawgs Untrusted Content Injection Surface Scanner™
tools.description: Scans one pasted blob of untrusted third-party content across six prompt-injection layers, quotes and explains every flag, and returns a quarantine verdict plus a stripped copy
tools.takes_in: One blob of untrusted content — a pasted document, web page text, tool output, or message the agent is about to act on
tools.hands_back: Every injection flag across six layers, quoted and explained, with a quarantine verdict — act on it, strip the flagged parts, or quarantine the whole blob

tools.name: J-Dawgs URL & Link Trust Auditor™
tools.description: Statically audits every URL in a draft for display-text mismatches, leaked token parameters, punycode/homoglyph hosts, brand-in-subdomain tricks, and hidden shortener destinations, using only brand pairs the user supplies; never fetches any URL
tools.takes_in: A draft containing URLs — a message, email, page, or post about to go out — plus your own brand → domain pairs: the brand names to protect and the domains that legitimately belong to each
tools.hands_back: A verdict for every link — SAFE, REVIEW, or DO NOT SEND — with the structural flags behind it: display-text mismatches, credentials and token parameters (values masked everywhere; cleaned URLs returned with them dropped), punycode and mixed-script hostnames decoded and flagged, brands riding in subdomains, shorteners marked destination-hidden, and login links over plain http

tools.name: J-Dawgs URL Encoding & Component Auditor™
tools.description: Batch-audits pasted URLs for double-encoding, raw characters, conflicting duplicate query keys, and embedded credentials (masked), returning cleaned URLs with a change receipt; never fetches
tools.takes_in: A pasted list of URLs — one per line, exactly as they are about to be handed over or published
tools.hands_back: Findings named per URL — double-encoding, raw spaces and unencoded characters, duplicate and conflicting duplicate query keys, embedded credentials (password never shown) — a cleaned URL with a per-change receipt, conflicts listed and never auto-resolved, and one verdict per URL: CLEAN / FIX BEFORE USE / DO NOT USE AS-IS

tools.name: J-Dawgs Vulnerability Report Triage Bench™
tools.description: Scanners list every finding flat; ours triages a pasted report by fix availability, exploit maturity, and reachability into one fix order — FIX FIRST / FIX SOON / SCHEDULE / NO FIX with a mitigation checklist / DEV-ONLY deprioritized, same CVE in multiple packages merged, unparsable lines reported by number, copyable fix plan + JSON export. Queries no live database; never invents a fixed version
tools.takes_in: A pasted vulnerability scanner report — the findings list as your scanner prints it: CVE or finding ID, package, installed and fixed versions where it gives them, severity, and any exploit or reachability notes it included
tools.hands_back: One fix order for the whole report — FIX FIRST / FIX SOON / SCHEDULE / NO FIX with a mitigation checklist / DEV-ONLY deprioritized, the same CVE in multiple packages merged into one group, and unparsable lines reported by number — plus a copyable fix plan and a JSON export

tools.name: J-Dawgs Webhook Contract Tester™
tools.description: Tests webhook deliveries against an expected contract: drift, duplicate event IDs, stale and out-of-order events, plus a dedupe list — now also audits pasted headers: signature presence (never claimed verified), a timestamp replay window with REPLAY RISK / HEADER RISK in the verdict, and secret-looking values masked
tools.takes_in: An expected contract payload, plus the actual webhook deliveries to test against it
tools.hands_back: A field-by-field diff — field drift and type changes — plus duplicate event IDs and stale and out-of-order timestamps, and a dedupe skip list of event IDs to drop on sight

tools.name: J-Dawgs Webhook Signature Verification Bench™
tools.description: Verify a captured webhook delivery offline (Stripe-style, GitHub-style, generic HMAC): SIGNATURE VALID / INVALID / CANNOT VERIFY plus a timestamp replay-risk check; the secret never leaves the browser and is never shown in output. Provider verification lives inside a server endpoint; ours verifies a captured delivery anywhere, offline, and grades the timestamp as a replay risk, not just the signature
tools.takes_in: A captured webhook delivery pasted in: the payload, its signature header, and the signing secret
tools.hands_back: SIGNATURE VALID / INVALID / CANNOT VERIFY for Stripe-style, GitHub-style, and generic HMAC schemes, plus a timestamp replay-risk check — the secret never leaves the browser and is never shown in the output

tools.name: J-Dawgs WebSocket Transcript Auditor™
tools.description: Audits a pasted WebSocket transcript: messages sent after close, unanswered pings, heartbeat gaps, malformed JSON frames, and oversized payloads are all flagged, and the audit returns one verdict — CLEAN SESSION / SESSION WITH ISSUES / BROKEN SESSION.
tools.takes_in: A pasted WebSocket transcript — frames with direction and timestamps, exactly as logged
tools.hands_back: A session report — post-close messages, unanswered pings, heartbeat gaps, malformed JSON frames, and oversized payloads named by line — and one session verdict

tools.name: J-Dawgs Whole-Request Token Estimator™
tools.description: Estimates a whole request's tokens — messages, tool schemas, and framing overhead together — with per-provider fit verdicts and an honest uncertainty band
tools.takes_in: A whole request payload as it will actually be sent — the messages, the tool schemas, and the provider or wrapper it is headed for
tools.hands_back: A token estimate for the whole payload, broken down by part — messages, tool schemas, wrapper overhead — with a per-provider fit verdict and the uncertainty band stated on the number

tools.name: J-Dawgs Workload Re-Pricer™
tools.description: Re-prices a pasted real usage export across seven model classes with cache and long-context tiers, prices stamped with their checked date
tools.takes_in: A pasted real usage export — the token counts, model names, cache hits, and request volumes from an actual run or billing period
tools.hands_back: The same workload priced across seven model classes with cache and long-context tiers applied, cheapest first, every price stamped with the date it was checked

tools.name: J-Dawgs Credential Compass™
tools.description: Verify your people's credentials without the paperwork chase. A two-sided guide for licensed trade workers and the businesses that hire them: workers learn what their credential is called, who issued it, and where the number lives (or how to give permission for a by-name pull); operators get the exact public record to check per trade, the six match fields, the three honest verdicts (PASS / FAIL / UNCONFIRMABLE = not verified), the pull-with-permission procedure with the never-guess collision rule, and a verification log entry builder.
